activities.title: A. Watch and Think (영상 시청 & 생각 나누기)

watchAndThink.videoTitle: CBS, Kids on the pressures of having a cell phone, social media at an early age
watchAndThink.sourceCitation: CBS, Kids on the pressures of having a cell phone, social media at an early age, 2022 (교과서 p.169 Sources)

script.speaker: M
script.en: Have you ever felt separation anxiety, when you didn’t have your phone in your hand or you didn’t have access to it?
script.ko: 손에 휴대폰이 없거나 사용할 수 없을 때 분리 불안을 느껴본 적이 있나요?

script.speaker: G1
script.en: In the past few years, it was like, when I would get my phone taken, I’d be like “Oh, I miss my phone. What am I going to do now?” I felt like I couldn’t live without it.
script.ko: 지난 몇 년 동안은 휴대폰을 빼앗기면 '아, 내 폰 그리워. 이제 뭐 하지?'라는 기분이었어요. 폰 없이 살 수 없을 것 같았죠.

script.speaker: B
script.en: I’ve definitely felt that, like, now my friends have, like, taken my phone when I was younger, and I would always get a little nervous about, like, “Where is my phone?” Like, that was the only thing on my mind when they took it.
script.ko: 저도 분명 그런 걸 느꼈어요. 어렸을 때 친구들이 폰을 가져가면 '내 폰 어디 있지?' 하고 항상 조금 불안해지곤 했죠. 친구들이 폰을 가져갔을 땐 머릿속에 그 생각뿐이었어요.

script.speaker: G2
script.en: I think I realized how impatient I’ve gotten when I don’t have it. And I can’t fill up the time with games or social media, things like that. And you’re just like “Oh, just stand and look around.”
script.ko: 휴대폰이 없을 때 제가 얼마나 안달하고 조급해지는지 깨달았어요. 게임이나 SNS 같은 것들로 시간을 채울 수도 없고요. 그냥 '아, 그냥 서서 주변이나 둘러보자' 하게 돼요.

activities.title: B. Listen and Answer (핵심 의사소통 대화)

dialogues.title: Dialogue 1: Where did the speakers decide to meet?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Hey, Jess, I’ve been meaning to ask you. When would be a good time to discuss promoting our club?
utterances.translation: 안녕, 제스, 물어보려던 참이었어. 우리 동아리 홍보 논의하기에 언제가 좋을까?

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: We’d better do it as soon as possible. I’m free after nine tonight.
utterances.translation: 가능한 한 빨리 하는 게 좋겠어. 난 오늘 밤 9시 이후에 시간 돼.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: That’s pretty late, isn’t it? How about meeting tomorrow morning at school?
utterances.translation: 꽤 늦은 시간이네, 그렇지 않아? 내일 아침에 학교에서 만나는 건 어때?

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: I don’t really feel like coming to school on the weekends. Why don’t we meet online tonight?
utterances.translation: 주말에 학교에 오고 싶진 않은데. 오늘 밤에 온라인으로 만나는 게 어때?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: I’m not sure about that. You know, when you talk online, it’s often hard to pay attention to what the other person is saying.
utterances.translation: 글쎄 잘 모르겠어. 온라인으로 이야기하면 상대방이 하는 말에 집중하기 어려울 때가 많잖아.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: I know what you mean, but by meeting online, we can discuss things comfortably at home late at night.
utterances.translation: 네가 무슨 말 하는지 이해하지만, 온라인으로 만나면 밤늦게 집에서 편하게 이야기할 수 있잖아.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Well, you’re right. I guess we’ll have to do it online this time.
utterances.translation: 음, 네 말이 맞아. 이번엔 온라인으로 해야겠네.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: Great. See you at nine.
utterances.translation: 좋아. 9시에 봐.

dialogues.title: Dialogue 2: What is the boy’s attitude toward working on his social media page?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: This chocolate cake looks fantastic!
utterances.translation: 이 초콜릿 케이크 정말 환상적이다!

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: Yeah, let’s dig in. I’m starving.
utterances.translation: 응, 어서 먹자. 나 배고파 죽겠어.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Wait a second! I need to take some pictures.
utterances.translation: 잠깐만! 사진 좀 찍어야 해.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: Wow, you’re taking a lot of photos. Are you going to use all of them?
utterances.translation: 와, 사진 진짜 많이 찍네. 그거 다 쓸 거야?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Of course not. I’m just going to keep the best ones for social media.
utterances.translation: 당연히 아니지. SNS용으로 제일 잘 나온 것만 남길 거야.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: You seem to be putting a lot of effort into it.
utterances.translation: 거기에 정말 공을 많이 들이는 것 같네.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Yeah, it’s not easy, but it really pays off when my photos get a lot of likes.
utterances.translation: 응, 쉽진 않지만 내 사진이 '좋아요'를 많이 받으면 정말 보람 있어.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: Which photo has gotten the most likes?
utterances.translation: 어떤 사진이 좋아요를 제일 많이 받았어?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Let me see .... So far, it’s the photo of my puppy wearing the sweater I made for him. Let me show you. Here.
utterances.translation: 어디 보자... 지금까지는 내가 떠준 스웨터를 입은 강아지 사진이야. 보여줄게. 여기.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: It’s super cute. Wow, look at all those comments under it!
utterances.translation: 엄청 귀엽다. 와, 밑에 댓글 달린 것 좀 봐!

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: I really like interacting with others on my social media site. That’s another reason I love social media.
utterances.translation: 내 SNS에서 다른 사람들과 소통하는 게 참 좋아. 그게 내가 SNS를 사랑하는 또 다른 이유야.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: That’s nice. I just hope you don’t spend too much time on it.
utterances.translation: 좋네. 너무 많은 시간만 쓰지 않길 바랄 뿐이야.

activities.title: C. Listen and Write (설문조사 5대 항목 그래프)

listenAndWrite.title: Main Reasons Why Social Media Is Considered Positive (Pew Research Center, 2022)

script.speaker: W
script.en: In our earlier survey, 420 teenagers in the U.S. said social media was mostly positive in their experience. We asked them why that was the case.
script.ko: 이전 설문조사에서 미국 십 대 420명은 SNS가 주로 긍정적인 경험이었다고 답했습니다. 우리는 그 이유를 물어보았습니다.

script.speaker: W
script.en: Nearly half mentioned the ability to build or maintain connections with others or to socialize on these platforms.
script.ko: 거의 절반이 타인과의 유대 관계를 형성하거나 유지하는 능력, 혹은 이러한 플랫폼에서 교류하는 능력을 언급했습니다.

script.speaker: W
script.en: A quarter of those said social media helped them learn or find information.
script.ko: 그중 4분의 1은 SNS가 정보를 배우거나 찾는 데 도움이 되었다고 말했습니다.

script.speaker: W
script.en: Meanwhile, 14% pointed to the entertainment value they saw in social media.
script.ko: 한편, 14%는 SNS에서 본 오락적 가치를 지목했습니다.

script.speaker: W
script.en: 7% of them explained that they used social media because they could focus on positive things on these platforms.
script.ko: 그들 중 7%는 이러한 플랫폼에서 긍정적인 것들에 집중할 수 있기 때문에 SNS를 사용한다고 설명했습니다.

activities.title: D. Write and Talk (Chance to Express)

dialogueModel.question: Do you think social media is harmful?
dialogueModel.positiveAnswer: Of course not. I think it’s useful because it helps me keep in touch with my friends.
dialogueModel.negativeAnswer: Yes, I do. I think it’s harmful because it makes it easy to spread misinformation.

activities.title: 본문 인터랙티브 리더 (Joy of Missing Out)

readingTip.title: Identifying with the writer (글쓴이와 동화되기)
readingTip.desc: Try to put yourself in the writer’s position. Relating to the writer’s emotions can help you better understand the text.

sentences.en: “Selena. SELENA!”
sentences.ko: “셀레나. 셀레나!”

sentences.en: “Yes,” I look up from my phone to discover my mom yelling at me.
sentences.ko: “네,” 나는 휴대폰에서 눈을 들어 엄마가 나에게 소리치고 계신 것을 발견한다.

sentences.en: She seems to be searching for an answer to something.
sentences.ko: 엄마는 무언가에 대한 답을 찾고 계신 듯하다.

sentences.en: “What?” I asked.
sentences.ko: “뭐라고요?” 내가 물었다.

sentences.en: She asked, “Did you not hear what I just said?”
sentences.ko: 엄마는 “내가 방금 한 말 못 들었니?”라고 물으셨다.

sentences.en: No, I didn’t. I didn’t hear anything she said.
sentences.ko: 아니요, 못 들었어요. 엄마가 하신 말씀은 아무것도 듣지 못했다.

sentences.en: I usually don’t hear a single word said to me by anyone.
sentences.ko: 나는 평소에 누구라도 나에게 하는 말을 단 한 마디도 듣지 못한다.

sentences.en: And why is that? It’s because my eyes are fixed on my phone.
sentences.ko: 그리고 왜 그럴까? 내 두 눈이 휴대폰에 고정되어 있기 때문이다.

sentences.en: My mom always asks me, “What is so interesting on your phone?”
sentences.ko: 엄마는 항상 나에게 물으신다, “네 폰에 뭐가 그렇게 재미있니?”

sentences.en: I never know how to answer that because even I don’t know what’s so interesting on my phone.
sentences.ko: 나조차도 내 폰에 뭐가 그리 재미있는지 모르기 때문에 나는 결코 어떻게 대답해야 할지 알지 못한다.

marginalQuestions.question: What is FOMO short for?
marginalQuestions.sampleAnswer: It is short for “fear of missing out.”

marginalQuestions.question: Why does Selena usually not hear what is said to her?
marginalQuestions.sampleAnswer: It is because her eyes are fixed on her phone.

sentences.en: I have a bad case of anxiety that comes from not checking my phone.
sentences.ko: 나는 휴대폰을 확인하지 않는 데서 오는 심각한 불안 증세를 가지고 있다.

sentences.en: I spend most of my day on social media.
sentences.ko: 나는 하루의 대부분을 SNS를 하며 보낸다.

sentences.en: I fear missing out on social media.
sentences.ko: 나는 SNS에서 소외되는 것을 두려워한다.

sentences.en: I fear not being in the know of what everyone is discussing.
sentences.ko: 나는 모두가 논의하고 있는 것을 알지 못할까 봐 두려워한다.

sentences.en: I fear not being in the know of what my friends are posting on social media.
sentences.ko: 나는 내 친구들이 SNS에 올리는 글을 알지 못할까 봐 두려워한다.

sentences.en: My mom thinks I’m addicted to my phone.
sentences.ko: 엄마는 내가 휴대폰에 중독되었다고 생각하신다.

sentences.en: Older people think teenagers like me have an addiction to their phones and computers.
sentences.ko: 어른들은 나 같은 십 대들이 휴대폰과 컴퓨터에 중독되었다고 생각한다.

sentences.en: But I wouldn’t say it’s an addiction to a device. It’s an addiction to social media.
sentences.ko: 하지만 나는 그것이 기기에 대한 중독이라고 말하지는 않겠다. 그것은 SNS에 대한 중독이다.

sentences.en: It’s an addiction to being online, or in other words, a fear of not being online.
sentences.ko: 그것은 온라인 상태에 있는 것에 대한 중독이며, 다시 말해 온라인 상태가 아닌 것에 대한 두려움이다.

sentences.en: Basically, I have severe FOMO, for which I’m in desperate need of a cure.
sentences.ko: 기본적으로 나는 극심한 FOMO를 앓고 있으며, 이에 대한 치유책이 절실히 필요하다.
sentences.grammarTip: 전치사 + 관계대명사: 'for which'는 앞의 severe FOMO를 수식하며 '그것에 대해 치료법이 절실히 필요한'으로 해석

sentences.en: Maybe this spring break could be a chance to find one.
sentences.ko: 어쩌면 이번 봄방학이 치료책을 찾을 기회가 될 수 있을 것이다.

marginalQuestions.question: How do Selena and her mother feel differently about her addiction?
marginalQuestions.sampleAnswer: Selena thinks that it is an addiction to social media, but her mother thinks that it is an addiction to her phone.

sentences.en: So it was time to pull the plug.
sentences.ko: 그래서 이제 플러그를 뽑을(접속을 끊을) 때가 되었다.

sentences.en: I grabbed my phone. I swiped it open and stared at the social media icons dotting the screen.
sentences.ko: 나는 휴대폰을 집어 들었다. 밀어서 잠금을 해제하고 화면에 흩어져 있는 SNS 아이콘들을 응시했다.

sentences.en: I removed the apps from my phone.
sentences.ko: 나는 휴대폰에서 그 앱들을 삭제했다.

sentences.en: Then I moved to my notebook computer. I logged out of all of the social media sites.
sentences.ko: 그러고 나서 노트북 컴퓨터로 옮겨갔다. 나는 모든 SNS 사이트에서 로그아웃했다.

sentences.en: I felt an immediate sense of relief.
sentences.ko: 나는 즉각적인 안도감을 느꼈다.

sentences.en: But soon after, I got restless.
sentences.ko: 하지만 얼마 지나지 않아 마음이 안절부절못해졌다.

sentences.en: I don’t remember how long it was, but I stared at my phone screen in complete confusion for quite a while.
sentences.ko: 얼마나 걸렸는지는 기억나지 않지만, 꽤 오랫동안 완벽한 혼란 속에서 휴대폰 화면을 응시했다.

sentences.en: I called Jamie, and we chatted for about an hour.
sentences.ko: 나는 제이미에게 전화했고, 우리는 한 시간가량 수다를 떨었다.

sentences.en: But there’s only so much you can do over a voice call. We decided to meet later in the afternoon for a bike ride.
sentences.ko: 하지만 음성 통화로 할 수 있는 것에는 한계가 있었다. 우리는 오후 늦게 자전거를 타러 만나기로 했다.

sentences.en: What else can I do on my phone? I lay on my bed even though I wasn’t sleepy.
sentences.ko: 내 폰으로 또 뭘 할 수 있을까? 졸리지 않았는데도 나는 침대에 누웠다.

sentences.en: I stayed there until I went out to meet Jamie.
sentences.ko: 나는 제이미를 만나러 나갈 때까지 그곳에 머물렀다.

sentences.en: Throughout the day, it felt like things slowed down considerably. What a long day!
sentences.ko: 하루 종일 시간이 상당히 느리게 흘러가는 것 같았다. 참 긴 하루였다!

marginalQuestions.question: What did Selena feel right after she “pulled the plug”?
marginalQuestions.sampleAnswer: She felt an immediate sense of relief.

marginalQuestions.question: What did Selena do right before going out to meet Jamie?
marginalQuestions.sampleAnswer: She lay on her bed even though she wasn’t sleepy.

sentences.en: I woke up late in the morning and reached for my phone.
sentences.ko: 아침에 늦게 일어나 휴대폰으로 손을 뻗었다.

sentences.en: I swiped my phone open only to remember my social media apps were no longer there.
sentences.ko: 휴대폰을 밀어서 열었지만, 내 SNS 앱이 더는 그곳에 없다는 것을 기억하게 되었을 뿐이다.

sentences.en: Old habits die hard.
sentences.ko: 오래된 습관은 쉽게 고쳐지지 않는다.

sentences.en: After breakfast, I felt a strong urge to go online, to which I didn’t want to give in.
sentences.ko: 아침 식사 후 온라인에 접속하고 싶은 강한 충동을 느꼈지만, 굴복하고 싶지 않았다.
sentences.grammarTip: 전치사 + 관계대명사: 'to which'는 앞의 urge(충동)를 수식하며 '그것에 굴복하고 싶지 않았던 충동'으로 해석

sentences.en: So, I decided to go out for a walk.
sentences.ko: 그래서 산책을 나가기로 결심했다.

sentences.en: While walking in the park, I probably glanced at my phone 20 times.
sentences.ko: 공원을 걷는 동안 나는 아마도 휴대폰을 스무 번은 힐끔거렸을 것이다.
sentences.grammarTip: 분사구문: 'While walking in the park'는 접속사가 생략되지 않은 분사구문으로 '공원을 걷는 동안'으로 해석

sentences.en: At one moment, I looked at the people around me, most of whom had their eyes glued to their phones.
sentences.ko: 어느 순간 주위를 둘러보았는데, 사람들 대부분이 휴대폰에 눈을 떼지 못하고 있었다.

sentences.en: I moved my gaze upward and noticed how purely blue the sky was, without a single cloud in sight.
sentences.ko: 시선을 위로 옮겨 구름 한 점 없이 하늘이 얼마나 순수하게 푸른지 알아챘다.

sentences.en: All around the park, trees slowly swayed back and forth. Soon I found myself taking a couple of pictures of the peaceful scene.
sentences.ko: 공원 사방에서 나무들이 천천히 앞뒤로 흔들리고 있었다. 곧 나는 그 평화로운 풍경 사진을 몇 장 찍고 있는 자신을 발견했다.

sentences.en: After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under my bed.
sentences.ko: 점심 식사 후, 침대 밑에서 오래된 기타를 꺼냈다.

readFurther.title: Volunteering Online
readFurther.source: Give a grad a go, Virtual volunteering ideas for students

paragraphs.text: Volunteering has a great deal of benefits. Not only do you make a positive impact on someone’s life, but you gain valuable skills for your career. It even reduces stress and anxiety. With busy schedules, it can be hard to find the time to commit to volunteer work. These days, however, you can make a huge difference in the lives of others from your own home by virtually volunteering. Here are a few ways to virtually volunteer.

First, you could be a part of the effort to lend support to senior citizens who struggle with loneliness. Typically, volunteer “phone friends” make regular calls to chat and check in with these people. Second, you can help people with low or no vision with their everyday tasks. Through a live video call, you can offer visual assistance to those who need it with tasks such as reading “use by” dates and instructions on food packages, which helps them to lead more independent lives. Finally, if you have an interest in wildlife and its conservation, you can help with animal monitoring work by watching live videos of animal habitats around the world. Monitoring these animals helps protect wildlife and develop methods of conserving them.

Helping others and giving back to the community can be very rewarding. It can make your day more meaningful and productive. It is also a great way to connect with new people and cultures. For those who believe in karma, if you do good things for others, good things will happen to you!

readFurther.question: Among the three ways of volunteering online, which would you like to try and why?
readFurther.sampleAnswer: I would like to become a phone friend for senior citizens because I like chatting with others and meeting new people.

modelWriting.title: Six Strings
modelWriting.text: Six Strings is a cool place where students can learn to play the guitar, discuss music, show their skills, and teach others. The club performs at school events at least twice a year, so you could get a chance to play on stage. How exciting is that? The club also sometimes participates in community events. You don’t have to bring a guitar; all you need is the willingness to interact with others. Don’t you want to make new friends while having fun playing the guitar and singing along? Come on and sign up now! You won’t regret it. #Six_Strings #school_club #fun_club #guitar #best_club For more information, contact 6strings@◯◯◯.hs.kr.
